title: Phenytoin: gingival hyperplasia (increased PDGF)
vignette: A 43-year-old male with multiple medical problems including a seizure disorder and mental illness comes to your office for the first time in order to establish a primary care physician. On routine physical examination, you notice the findings shown in the photo: marked overgrowth of the gingival (gum) tissue partially covering the teeth. Which of the following is most likely responsible for the condition of this patient's teeth and gums?

clues.note: A chronic seizure disorder is often treated with phenytoin, an anticonvulsant classically associated with gingival hyperplasia.

clues.text: marked overgrowth of the gingival (gum) tissue partially covering the teeth
clues.note: Gingival hyperplasia (gum overgrowth) is a classic, characteristic adverse effect of long-term phenytoin therapy.

whatMatters: Gum overgrowth (gingival hyperplasia) in a patient on chronic antiepileptic therapy for a seizure disorder is the classic adverse effect of PHENYTOIN. It results from increased platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) stimulating gingival cell/alveolar proliferation. Answer A. (It may regress after stopping the drug.)
strategy: Match the classic finding to the drug: phenytoin -> gingival hyperplasia (also hirsutism, coarse facies, megaloblastic anemia, ataxia/nystagmus, P450 induction, fetal hydantoin syndrome). Reject drugs that don't cause gum overgrowth: lithium (tremor, nephrogenic DI, hypothyroidism), prednisone (hyperglycemia/edema/osteoporosis), cocaine (ischemia/seizures), methimazole (agranulocytosis), and clozapine (agranulocytosis, seizures). (Note: calcium channel blockers and cyclosporine also cause gingival hyperplasia, but they aren't listed.)

eliminations.label: Lithium - tremor/nephrogenic DI/thyroid, not gums
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a mood stabilizer with a narrow therapeutic index. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: lithium toxicity causes tremor, ataxia, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, and cardiac conduction defects - not gingival hyperplasia. ✅ Correct if: lithium toxicity (tremor/DI/hypothyroidism).

eliminations.label: Prednisone - Cushingoid effects, not gum overgrowth
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a glucocorticoid. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes hyperglycemia, weight gain, edema, osteoporosis, and immunosuppression - not gingival hyperplasia. ✅ Correct if: Cushingoid/steroid adverse effects.

eliminations.label: Cocaine - ischemia/seizures, not gingival hyperplasia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a sympathomimetic stimulant. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes vasoconstriction/ischemia, hypertension, and seizures (and nasal septal/dental erosion from use), not the characteristic gingival overgrowth of phenytoin. ✅ Correct if: cocaine cardiovascular/CNS toxicity.

eliminations.label: Methimazole - agranulocytosis, not gums
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an antithyroid drug (inhibits thyroid peroxidase). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its serious adverse effect is agranulocytosis (also rash, edema), not gingival hyperplasia. ✅ Correct if: hyperthyroidism treatment with agranulocytosis risk.

eliminations.label: Clozapine - agranulocytosis/seizures, not gum overgrowth
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an atypical antipsychotic for refractory schizophrenia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its hallmark toxicities are agranulocytosis (monitored) and seizures, not gingival hyperplasia. ✅ Correct if: refractory schizophrenia with agranulocytosis monitoring.

reasoning: Seizure disorder + gingival hyperplasia = classic phenytoin adverse effect
Phenytoin increases platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) expression
PDGF stimulates proliferation of gingival cells and alveolar bone -> gum overgrowth
mechanism: Phenytoin is an anticonvulsant that blocks voltage-gated sodium channels to suppress abnormal neuronal firing (used for tonic-clonic, partial, and status epilepticus). It has a narrow therapeutic index and numerous adverse effects, the most characteristic mucocutaneous one being GINGIVAL HYPERPLASIA, occurring in roughly half of patients after months of therapy: phenytoin increases expression of PLATELET-DERIVED GROWTH FACTOR (PDGF), and gingival macrophages exposed to PDGF stimulate proliferation of gingival fibroblasts and alveolar bone, producing gum overgrowth (which may regress if the drug is stopped, with good oral hygiene). Other phenytoin effects include hirsutism and coarsening of facial features, megaloblastic anemia (impaired folate metabolism), cerebellar/vestibular toxicity (ataxia, nystagmus), P450 INDUCTION (drug interactions), Stevens-Johnson syndrome/DRESS, osteopenia, and fetal hydantoin syndrome. Among the options only phenytoin causes gingival hyperplasia (as do calcium channel blockers like nifedipine and cyclosporine, which aren't listed). The distractors have unrelated toxicity profiles.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Pharm/Neuro > phenytoin: Na-channel blocker; adverse effects = gingival hyperplasia (↑PDGF), hirsutism, coarse facies, megaloblastic anemia, ataxia/nystagmus, P450 induction, fetal hydantoin syndrome, SJS.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Gum overgrowth + seizure disorder = phenytoin (PDGF-driven gingival hyperplasia).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on gingival hyperplasia, platelet-derived growth factor, P450 induction, or fetal hydantoin syndrome? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Lithium (tremor/DI), prednisone (Cushingoid), cocaine (ischemia), methimazole/clozapine (agranulocytosis) don't cause gum overgrowth.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the photo: markedly enlarged, overgrown gingival tissue partially covering the teeth = gingival hyperplasia. Anchor: 'gum overgrowth + seizures = phenytoin.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: phenytoin -> gingival hyperplasia (↑PDGF); also hirsutism, megaloblastic anemia, ataxia, P450 induction (CCBs/cyclosporine also cause gingival hyperplasia).
